clue.text: Secure business (technical) held parties!

indicators.note: read as a verb, parties means goes wild and celebrates, so the letters of the two preceding words are thrown about

explanation.surface: A deal is done at a technical meeting and everyone celebrates with parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parties' is a verb here, the anagram signal: the letters of TECHNICAL and HELD are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure a business agreement is to finalise it, the idiom for completing a transaction.

clue.text: TV personality, person revered on old Scottish island, blocks some light

indicators.note: the inner pieces block, or sit in the middle of, the unit of light that surrounds them

parts.note: the lux is a unit of illumination, a measured amount of light

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits below it, so this piece comes after

parts.note: Uist is an island in the Outer Hebrides of Scotland
a hero is a person admired and revered

explanation.surface: A television presenter, worshipped on a historic Scottish island, stands in the way of the light.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed below, so the hero follows the old island; 'blocks' has that run sit inside the unit of light, as though blocking it.
explanation.definitionFit: This documentary maker is a well-known British television presenter.

clue.text: Shiva's bull or bear — do they unite Ulster?

indicators.note: the question asks whether the joining word sits between the two letters for Northern Ireland, placing it inside them

parts.note: Ulster is commonly used for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI
the conjunction 'and' is the word that unites two things

explanation.surface: A question about whether Hindu symbols or animals could bring Ulster together.
explanation.walkthrough: N and I, the initials of Northern Ireland, are united by AND placed between them. The Nandi bear is a legendary creature of Kenyan folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiva's mount in Hindu mythology is a bull of that name, and a cryptid of East Africa shares it.

clue.text: Normal location of animal partially obscured by tile?

indicators.note: the piece that is obscured is covered and enclosed by the headgear around it

parts.note: tile is old slang for a hat
partially means to some extent, a bit

explanation.surface: An animal's home is half hidden by a roof tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tile' is old slang for a hat; 'obscured by' puts A BIT inside HAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural home or environment of a creature is where it is normally found.

clue.text: An inside Noah's redesigned, praise the Lord!

indicators.note: the short word goes within the rearranged letters of the patriarch's name
something redesigned is put together in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of praise from someone who has rebuilt Noah's ark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redesigned' is the anagram signal on the patriarch's name, possessive S included; 'inside' sets the short word in its middle. The exclamation is the definition, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a liturgical shout of adoration to God, used in hymns and the Bible.

clue.text: Poor players initially deft playing the piano?

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word deft

parts.note: a pianist plays on keys, so 'on keys' describes playing the piano

explanation.surface: Deft performers at the piano, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Donkeys' is British slang for hopeless sportsmen, hence 'Poor players'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British sporting slang, weak or clumsy performers are called by the name of a stubborn beast of burden.

clue.text: Four in a car go to sleep in the heat of the moment?

definitions.text: go to sleep in the heat of the moment?

indicators.note: the numeral goes inside the word for the car

parts.note: an estate is a British estate car, a station wagon
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people crammed into a car nod off in the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: An estate car is the British station wagon. The definition plays on 'heat of the moment' to mean a hot season.
explanation.definitionFit: Some animals spend summer dormant, the hot-weather counterpart of hibernation.

clue.text: Jiggery-pokery in Jongleurs

definitions.meaning: jiggery-pokery means trickery or underhand dealing
Jongleurs is a British chain of comedy clubs, where the trade is comic

explanation.surface: Dishonest goings-on at a comedy club.
explanation.walkthrough: Jongleurs was a well-known chain of British stand-up comedy clubs, so its trade is literally comic business.
explanation.definitionFit: Trickery is suspicious conduct, and a comedy club's trade is literally humorous commerce.

clue.text: Bad men moor ships with his dough, in utter exasperation?

indicators.note: bad suggests something gone wrong, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Inept sailors tie up their boats, a costly and exasperating business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges MEN MOOR SHIPS. 'his dough' sounds like the cartoon character's catchphrase 'D'oh!', uttered in exasperation.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon father's famous exclamation of frustration is 'D'oh!', punned here as dough.

clue.text: I help to produce paper giving thanks in new-format dissertations

indicators.note: the short word for thanks goes inside the rearranged letters
dissertations put into a new format have their letters rearranged

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone who helps produce a paper, thanking contributors in revised dissertations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new-format' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion; 'giving' only links. The definition is spoken in the first person, as a riddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A subordinate journalist helps put a newspaper together, so speaks of themselves this way.

clue.text: Actor who derides churchgoer?

parts.note: a churchgoer is a Christian
to slate is to criticise harshly, so one who derides is a slater

explanation.surface: A performer who mocks religious believers.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'slate' is British for criticising harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of an American film performer.

clue.text: Arctic craft — this would moor one, or chance drifting

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: drifting suggests letters floating out of place, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Arctic vessel needs something to tie it up, or it may drift away.
explanation.walkthrough: I (one) is followed by 'drifting', which rearranges OR and CHANCE to CEANCHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar ships fasten themselves to floes using this kind of mooring device.

clue.text: New table on which to consume more liqueur

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
a chart is a table of information
to reuse is to use again, to consume more

explanation.surface: A new table where diners can drink more liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a herbal spirit made by Carthusian monks in the French Alps.

clue.text: One imitates Officer Dibble and TC, say, around yard

indicators.note: the two cartoon figures surround the abbreviation for yard

parts.note: Officer Dibble is the policeman in the cartoon Top Cat, a cop
TC is Top Cat, an example of a cat

explanation.surface: Someone mimics the cartoon policeman and Top Cat as they patrol the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: In the US cartoon Top Cat, TC is the alley cat and Officer Dibble the policeman who chases him; 'around' has the pair wrap the yard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A mimic who copies others is given this childish label.

clue.text: Greenfly henchmen noticed around pub

indicators.note: the henchmen are seen hanging about the pub, so they surround it

parts.note: henchmen are aides, a boss's assistants
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A boss's minions are spotted loitering near the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: PH (public house) is a common British abbreviation for a pub; 'noticed around' puts it inside AIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly are sap-sucking garden insects, and this is a plural of aphis.

clue.text: Following rising tax near resorts, stay here in Greece

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the upturned tax
in a down clue, rising means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: resorts as a verb means sorts again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: With taxes rising near holiday resorts, this is where to stay in Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the tax upwards in this down clue; 'resorts' is read as 'sorts again', an anagram signal, not holiday towns; 'Following' places that anagram after the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek tavern or small inn is a place to eat, drink or lodge on holiday.

clue.text: Reference book to make more sound?

definitions.meaning: read as an instruction, find or consult the book: to turn up is to locate
to increase the loudness on a radio or stereo

explanation.surface: A reference book that makes things louder.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising the loudness is the idiom; read literally the phrase means finding a tome.

clue.text: Asian clothing one, after having taken a breather

indicators.note: the numeral comes after the breathing organ

parts.note: a lung is an organ that breathes
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An Asian garment donned once someone has taken a breather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a breather' looks like a rest; it is the organ LUNG. A lungi is a sarong-like cloth worn in South Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: This sarong-style wrap is worn round the waist in India, Bangladesh and Myanmar.

clue.text: Time knickers had to be changed before Saturday, leading to gloom

indicators.note: the rest of the letters come before the abbreviation for Saturday
the letters of the underwear and the verb are changed into a new order

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for Saturday

explanation.surface: Someone must change their underwear before Saturday night, heading into a gloomy mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be changed' is the anagram signal and 'before' places the Saturday letter last; 'leading to' only links. Knickers is British for women's underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep obscurity, a biblical phrase for profound blackness, is utter gloom.

clue.text: What have been declared for Zimbabwe/Bangladesh (most recently), or England/Australia (not new)?

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: not tells us to take away the letter for new

parts.note: these countries all play Test cricket, the newest and oldest Test nations

explanation.surface: A cricket question about which countries have declared, recent arrivals or old rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: Test cricket is the five-day international form; England and Australia were the first Test nations, Zimbabwe and Bangladesh recent additions. 'declared' also plays on a cricket declaration.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn assertions or objections are statements that people make formally.
